the guidelines or the amendment or notice of the
revocation (as the case requires) to be given to the
Attorney-General.

history.raw: S. 16C inserted by No. 19/2005 s. 5.

nodes.text:
The Chief Magistrate may, at any time,
having regard to any guidelines in force under
section 16B(1), recommend to the Attorney-
General that a judicial registrar, or more than one
judicial registrar, of the Court be appointed by the
Governor in Council.

The Attorney-General, on receiving a
recommendation under subsection (1), may
recommend to the Governor in Council that a
judicial registrar, or more than one judicial
registrar, of the Court be appointed under
subsection (3).

history.raw: S. 16C(2) amended by No. 34/2010 s. 50.

nodes.text:
The Governor in Council, on the recommendation
of the Attorney-General, may appoint a person as
a judicial registrar of the Court for the period, not
exceeding 5 years, specified in his or her
instrument of appointment.

A person is not eligible for appointment as a
judicial registrar unless he or she is—
an Australian lawyer; or

history.raw: S. 16C(4)(a) substituted by No. 19/2005 s. 6, amended by No. 17/2014 s. 160(Sch. 2 item 59.3).

nodes.text:
enrolled as a legal practitioner of the High
Court of Australia.

A judicial registrar may be appointed on a
full-time or part-time basis.

A judicial registrar, although not appointed on a
part-time basis, may, by agreement in writing
entered into with the Chief Magistrate, undertake
the duties of a judicial registrar on a part-time
basis.

A judicial registrar is eligible for re-appointment
in accordance with this section if the Chief
Magistrate recommends to the Attorney-General
that the person be re-appointed.

history.raw: S. 16C(7) amended by No. 62/2014 s. 91.

nodes.text:
The Public Administration Act 2004 does not
apply to a judicial registrar in respect of the office
of judicial registrar.

history.raw: S. 16D inserted by No. 19/2005 s. 5.

nodes.text:
A judicial registrar is entitled to the terms and
conditions including remuneration and allowances
that are fixed in respect of him or her from time to
time by the Governor in Council.

history.raw: S. 16D(1) amended by No. 29/2015 s. 70(1).

nodes.text:
Except with the approval of the Attorney-General,
a judicial registrar must not engage in legal
practice, undertake paid employment or conduct a
business, trade or profession of any kind.

A judicial registrar must disclose to the Chief
Magistrate in writing any direct or indirect
pecuniary interest that he or she has or acquires
that could conflict with the proper performance of
the duties of the office of judicial registrar.

Despite any provision to the contrary made by or
under any other Act, a person who has held the
office of judicial registrar is entitled to have his or
her service in that office taken into account in
computing the period of service which entitles
public officials (within the meaning of the Public
Administration Act 2004) to be granted long
service leave or other leave entitlements, whether
his or her service in the office of judicial registrar
is before or after any period of service as such a
public official.

The following are to be paid out of the
Consolidated Fund, which is appropriated to the
necessary extent—

history.raw: S. 16D(5) inserted by No. 29/2015 s. 70(2).

nodes.text:
the amounts (including the amount of any
non-salary benefits) payable to or for any
judicial registrar; and

premiums and other amounts payable under
the Workplace Injury Rehabilitation and
Compensation Act 2013 in respect of any
judicial registrar; and

payroll tax payable under the Payroll Tax
Act 2007 in respect of wages paid or payable
to any judicial registrar; and

tax payable under the Fringe Benefits Tax
Act 1986 of the Commonwealth in respect of
fringe benefits provided to any judicial
registrar; and

superannuation contributions within the
meaning of the Payroll Tax Act 2007
payable in respect of any judicial registrar.

In this section, non-salary benefits has the same
meaning as it has in clause 3(5) and (6) of
Schedule 1A to the Public Administration
Act 2004.

history.raw: S. 16D(6) inserted by No. 29/2015 s. 70(2).

nodes.text:
Nothing in this section authorises the salary or the
aggregate value of the allowances payable to a
judicial registrar to be reduced.

history.raw: S. 16D(7) inserted by No. 62/2014 s. 92.
S. 16DB inserted by No. 62/2014 s. 93.

nodes.text:
A judicial registrar must take an oath or
affirmation of office in the prescribed form and
manner.

Subsection (1) only applies to a person who is
appointed or re-appointed as a judicial registrar on
or after the commencement of section 93 of the
Courts Legislation Miscellaneous Amendments
Act 2014.

A failure by a person to take an oath or
affirmation of office in accordance with this
section does not invalidate anything done by that
person as a judicial registrar.

nodes.heading: Resignation from office
nodes.text:
A judicial registrar may resign from office by
delivering to the Governor a signed letter of
resignation.

history.raw: S. 16E inserted by No. 19/2005 s. 5.

nodes.heading: Rules of Court
nodes.text:
The Chief Magistrate together with one or more
Deputy Chief Magistrates may jointly make rules
of court for or with respect to—

history.raw: S. 16I inserted by No. 19/2005 s. 5, amended by No. 20/2022 s. 35.

nodes.text:
delegating to the judicial registrars all or any
of the powers of the Court except the
power—

history.raw: S. 16I(b)(ii) repealed by No. 65/2011 s. 107(Sch. item 8.1).

nodes.text:
to impose a sentence of imprisonment
or of detention in a youth justice centre
or youth residential centre; or

history.raw: S. 16I(b)(i) amended by No. 48/2006 s. 42(Sch. item 22.2).

nodes.text:
to make a drug and alcohol treatment
order within the meaning of the
Sentencing Act 1991; or

history.raw: S. 16I(b)(iii) amended by No. 43/2020 s. 38.

nodes.text:
to make a Court Secure Treatment
Order within the meaning of the
Sentencing Act 1991; or

history.raw: S. 16I(b)(iv) amended by No. 69/2005 s. 28, substituted by No. 26//2014 s. 455(Sch. item 20.2).

nodes.text:
to hear and determine an appeal made
to the Court; or

history.raw: S. 16I(b)(v) amended by No. 65/2011 s. 107(Sch. item 8.2).
S. 16I(b)(vi) inserted by No. 65/2011 s. 107(Sch. item 8.3), amended by No. 62/2014 s. 94(a).

nodes.text:
reviews of, and appeals from, the court
constituted by a judicial registrar.

history.raw: S. 16I(c) inserted by No. 62/2014 s. 94(b).

nodes.heading: Performance of duties by judicial registrar

history.raw: S. 16J inserted by No. 19/2005 s. 5.

nodes.text:
A judicial registrar must not hear, or continue to
hear, a proceeding that the judicial registrar
considers for any reason inappropriate for hearing
and determination by the Court constituted by a
judicial registrar and must make appropriate
arrangements for the proceeding to be heard and
determined by the Court constituted by a
magistrate.

A judicial registrar, in the performance of his or
her duties as a judicial registrar, is not subject to
the direction or control of any person or body.

A judicial registrar has, in the performance of his
or her duties as a judicial registrar, the same
protection and immunity as a Judge of the
Supreme Court has in the performance of his or
her duties as a Judge.

A judicial registrar has any of the powers, duties
and functions of a registrar under this Act and any
other Act or the Rules.

history.raw: S. 16J(4) inserted by No. 17/2023 s. 36.

nodes.heading: Appeal from or review of determination of Court constituted by judicial registrar

history.raw: S. 16K inserted by No. 19/2005 s. 5, substituted by No. 62/2014 s. 95.

nodes.text:
The rules may provide for appeals from or
reviews of a determination of the Court
constituted by a judicial registrar—
whether in respect of—
any interlocutory application; and

whether in respect of specified kinds of
application or proceeding or generally; and

by specifying whether the procedure is by
way of appeal or review or both; and

by specifying the way in which the Court
may be constituted for those appeals or
reviews.

The powers in subsection (1) are in addition to
and do not limit any power to make rules under
section 16I.

Unless the rules otherwise provide, a
determination of the Court constituted by a
judicial registrar may be appealed from or
reviewed—

on application of a party to the proceeding;
or
on the Court's own motion.

If the rules do not provide for an appeal from or a
review of a determination of the Court constituted
by a judicial registrar, the determination is to be
subject to a review or an appeal conducted—

by way of hearing de novo by the Court
constituted by a magistrate; and

otherwise in accordance with the rules, if
any.

nodes.heading: Employment of principal registrar, registrars and deputy registrars

history.raw: S. 17(1A)(1B) inserted by No. 10/1999 s. 23, amended by No. 108/2004 s. 117(1) (Sch. 3 item 118.2), repealed by No. 1/2014 s. 72.

nodes.text:
For the purposes of this Act and to assist in the
administration of the Court there are to be
employed under Part 3 of the Public
Administration Act 2004—
a principal registrar; and

as many registrars and deputy registrars as
are necessary.

The principal registrar, registrars and deputy
registrars have the duties, powers and functions
provided by this Act and the Fines Reform
Act 2014, the regulations and the Rules.

The principal registrar may, by instrument,
delegate to any registrar or class of registrars any
function or power of the principal registrar under
this Act and the Fines Reform Act 2014, the
regulations or the Rules, except this power of
delegation.

A deputy registrar may, subject to this Act, the
regulations and the Rules and to any directions of
a registrar, exercise any of the powers or perform
any of the functions of a registrar.

nodes.heading: Appointment of Aboriginal elders or respected persons

history.raw: S. 17A inserted by No. 27/2002 s. 7.

nodes.text:
The Chief Executive Officer may appoint a person
who is a member of the Aboriginal community as
an Aboriginal elder or respected person for the
purpose of performing functions in relation to the
Koori Court Division of the Court as set out in
this Act.

history.raw: S. 17A(1) amended by No. 3/2016 s. 3(1).

nodes.text:
An Aboriginal elder or respected person holds
office for the period, and on the terms and
conditions, determined by the Chief Executive
Officer and specified in the instrument of
appointment.

history.raw: S. 17A(2) amended by No. 3/2016 s. 3(1).

nodes.text:
An Aboriginal elder or respected person may
resign from office by writing signed by him or her
and delivered to the Chief Executive Officer.

history.raw: S. 17A(3) amended by No. 3/2016 s. 3(1).

nodes.text:
In this section—
Chief Executive Officer means the Chief
Executive Officer of Court Services Victoria
appointed under section 22 of the Court
Services Victoria Act 2014.

history.raw: S. 17A(4) inserted by No. 3/2016 s. 3(2).

nodes.text:
The principal registrar must cause a register to be
kept of all the orders of the Court and of such
other matters as are directed by this Act or the
Rules to be entered in the register.

An order made by the Court must be authenticated
by the person who constituted the Court.

Any person may, subject to any order made under
Part 3 of the Open Courts Act 2013 and on
payment of the prescribed fee, inspect that part of
the register that contains the final orders of the
Court.

history.raw: S. 18(3) amended by No. 58/2013 s. 49.

nodes.text:
A party to a proceeding may inspect without
charge that part of the register that relates to that
proceeding.

A document purporting to be an extract from the
register and purporting to be signed by a registrar
who certifies that in his or her opinion the extract
is a true extract from the register is admissible in
evidence in any proceedings and, in the absence of
evidence to the contrary, is proof of the matters
appearing in the extract.

nodes.heading: Offence to publish certain information concerning proceedings
nodes.text:
A person must not, in the course of a business of
publishing information concerning debtors,
publish or cause to be published any information
concerning the commencement of a proceeding
for debt so as to identify the defendant before a
final order is made in the proceeding.
Penalty: 100 penalty units.

nodes.heading: Recording of proceedings
nodes.text:
The principal registrar must ensure that all
proceedings in the Court are recorded in
accordance with the Rules.

history.raw: S. 19A inserted by No. 51/2000 s. 5.

nodes.text:
Process may only be issued out of the Court by a
registrar, except where otherwise provided by or
under this or any other Act.

The principal registrar must, subject to the
regulations, keep the original of all process issued
out of the Court and must issue or cause to be
issued as many copies as are necessary.

Process issued by a registrar may be recalled and
cancelled by—
that registrar; or

if that registrar is dead or has ceased to hold
office or cannot be located, a magistrate.

A registrar has the following powers in addition to
those conferred on him or her by this or any other
Act or the Rules—
power to issue any process out of the Court;
power to administer an oath or affirmation;

history.raw: S. 21(1)(b) amended by No. 6/2018 s. 68(Sch. 2 item 81.1).

nodes.text:
power to endorse a warrant to arrest in
accordance with section 62;

power to sign any licence or certificate
which the Court is authorised to issue;

power to hear and determine any application,
and exercise any power or authority of the
Court, under section 58, 59 or 60 of the
Supreme Court Act 1986;

power to make a declaration under
Division 4 of Part 7 of the National
Domestic Violence Order Scheme
Act 2016;

history.raw: S. 21(1)(g) inserted by No. 53/2016 s. 109(b), amended by No. 11/2021 s. 54(1)(b).

nodes.text:
power to adjourn a criminal proceeding or a
proceeding under the Family Violence
Protection Act 2008, the Personal Safety
Intervention Orders Act 2010 or the
National Domestic Violence Order
Scheme Act 2016;

power to abridge or extend the adjournment
of a criminal proceeding or a proceeding
under the Family Violence Protection
Act 2008, the Personal Safety Intervention
Orders Act 2010 or the National Domestic
Violence Order Scheme Act 2016;

power to otherwise change the time or place
at which a criminal proceeding or a
proceeding under the Family Violence
Protection Act 2008, the Personal Safety
Intervention Orders Act 2010 or the
National Domestic Violence Order
Scheme Act 2016 is listed before the Court.

Nothing in this section empowers a registrar to
vary the amount or conditions of bail.

The power under subsection (1)(c) to abridge or
extend the bail of a person may be exercised—

history.raw: S. 21(3) inserted by No. 11/2021 s. 54(3).

nodes.text:
at any time, including on the day on which
the person's proceeding is listed before the
Court; and

either in the presence or absence of the
person.

The powers under subsection (1)(h), (i) and (j) in
respect of a proceeding may be exercised—

history.raw: S. 21(4) inserted by No. 11/2021 s. 54(3).

nodes.text:
at any time, including on the day on which
the proceeding is listed before the Court; and

either in the presence or absence of the
parties.

The powers under subsection (1)(c), (h), (i) and (j)
may be exercised—

history.raw: S. 21(5) inserted by No. 11/2021 s. 54(3).

nodes.text: on the application of a party; or
on the registrar's own initiative.

history.raw: S. 22 amended by No. 9/1995 s. 11(3)(a).

nodes.text:
Subject to subsection (2), a registrar must demand
and receive the prescribed fees.

Subject to the regulations or any power to waive,
postpone, remit or refund a prescribed fee in a
civil proceeding, the appropriate registrar may,
having regard to the income, day to day living
expenses, liabilities and assets of the person liable
to pay the fee, waive payment of that fee if, in his
or her opinion, the payment of that fee by that
person would cause him or her financial hardship
and, in that case, that prescribed fee is not
payable.

history.raw: S. 22(2) inserted by No. 9/1995 s. 11(3)(b), amended by No. 15/2018 s. 47.

nodes.text:
Subsections (1) and (2) do not apply to fees
payable to the sheriff.

history.raw: S. 22(3) inserted by No. 64/1996 s. 32.

nodes.heading: Extortion by and impersonation of court officials
nodes.text:
The following persons are guilty of an offence and
liable to a fine of not more than 20 penalty units
or to imprisonment for a term of not more than
2 years or to both—

any person who is not a court official and
who pretends to be a court official.

nodes.heading: Protection of registrars
nodes.text:
The principal registrar, a registrar and a deputy
registrar have, in the performance of their duties
in good faith, the same protection and immunity
as a magistrate has in the performance of his or
her duties as a magistrate.

history.raw: S. 24 amended by No. 64/2010 s. 64.

nodes.text: The Court has jurisdiction—

to hear and determine all summary offences;
and

to hear and determine all indictable offences
which may be heard and determined
summarily; and

to conduct committal proceedings into
indictable offences and either—

direct the accused to be tried and order
that the accused be remanded in
custody until trial or grant bail; or

history.raw: S. 25(1)(c)(i) amended by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 82.25).

nodes.text:
discharge the accused under section
126(4) of the Criminal Procedure
Act 2009; and

to make orders to enforce the payment of all
fines which are, by any Act, directed to be
recovered in the Court or for the recovery of
which no provision is made.

The jurisdiction given by subsection (1) is
additional to any other jurisdiction given to the
Court with respect to a criminal proceeding by or
under any Act other than this Act.

In a particular case, the jurisdiction given by
subsection (1)(c) may be exercised concurrently
with the jurisdiction of the Children's Court to
conduct a committal proceeding if—

history.raw: S. 25(3) inserted by No. 7/2009 s. 426 (as amended by No. 68/2009 ss 46(a), 54(l)).

nodes.text: the accused who is a child—

is of or over the age of 15 years at the
time the proceeding against the child
for the offence is commenced; and

is charged with murder, attempted
murder, manslaughter, child homicide,
homicide by firearm, a designated
offence (within the meaning of
section 516 of the Children, Youth
and Families Act 2005) committed
when the child was aged 15 years or
over, an offence against section 197A
of the Crimes Act 1958 (arson causing
death) or an offence against section 318
of the Crimes Act 1958 (culpable
driving causing death); and

the Court makes an order under
subsection (4) in relation to the accused who
is not a child and the Children's Court makes
an order under section 516A(2) of the
Children, Youth and Families Act 2005 in
relation to the accused who is a child.

The Court may order that joint committal
proceedings in relation to a particular accused are
appropriate having regard to—

history.raw: S. 25(4) inserted by No. 7/2009 s. 426 (as amended by No. 68/2009 ss 46(b), 54(l)).

nodes.text: the age of the child; and

the effect on victims of the offence charged
if the committal proceedings were not
conducted jointly; and

the estimated duration of the committal
proceedings if conducted jointly; and

the number of witnesses that would be
cross-examined by both accused; and
any other matter considered relevant.

The Court may make an order under
subsection (4) on the application of a party or on
its own motion.

history.raw: S. 25(5) inserted by No. 7/2009 s. 426 (as amended by No. 68/2009 s. 54(l)).

nodes.text:
Each party is entitled to be present and may
address the Court when the Court is considering
the making of an order under subsection (4).

history.raw: S. 25(6) inserted by No. 7/2009 s. 426 (as amended by No. 68/2009 s. 54(l)).

nodes.text:
If the Court makes an order under subsection (4),
the Court may adjourn the proceeding for a period
not exceeding 28 days to enable the Children's
Court to determine whether joint committal
proceedings are appropriate in the particular case.

history.raw: S. 25(7) inserted by No. 7/2009 s. 426 (as amended by No. 68/2009 s. 54(l)).

nodes.text:
If joint committal proceedings are conducted
under subsection (3)—
with any necessary modifications to ensure that
the joint committal proceedings are conducted
fairly and efficiently.

history.raw: S. 25(8) inserted by No. 7/2009 s. 426 (as amended by No. 68/2009 ss 46(c), 54(l)).

nodes.text:
the Children, Youth and Families
Act 2005 applies as far as practicable to
the child; and

the Criminal Procedure Act 2009 applies
as far as practicable to the other accused—

history.raw: Pt 4 Div. 2 (Heading) repealed by No. 7/2009 s. 427(1)(c) (as amended by No. 68/2009 s. 54(m)).
Pt 4 Div. 2 Subdiv. 1 (Heading) repealed by No. 7/2009 s. 427(1)(c) (as amended by No. 68/2009 s. 54(m)).
Pt 4 Div. 2 (Heading) inserted by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 82.26).
Pt 4 Div. 2 Subdiv. 2 (Heading) repealed by No. 7/2009 s. 427(1)(c) (as amended by No. 68/2009 s. 54(m)).

Pt 4 Div. 2 Subdiv. 4 (Heading and s. 56) amended by Nos 64/1990 s. 20(Sch. item 4.2), 43/1994 s. 56(Sch. item 3.1), 10/1999 ss 5, 8(2)(3), 92/2000 ss 5, 6, 48/2006 s. 42(Sch. item 22.4), 50/2006 ss 24, 25, repealed by No. 7/2009 s. 427(1)(c) (as amended by No. 68/2009 s. 54(m)).

nodes.heading: Magistrate may exercise registrar's powers
nodes.text:
A magistrate may exercise any of the powers of a
registrar for the purpose of issuing criminal
process.

The Court or a registrar may issue the following
witness summonses—
summons to give evidence;

history.raw: S. 43(9)(a) repealed by No. 69/2009 s. 54(Sch. Pt 1 item 34.3).

nodes.text: summons to produce documents or things;

summons to give evidence and produce
documents or things.

Any party to a criminal proceeding in the Court
may apply for the issue of a witness summons.

A witness summons may be directed to any
person who appears to the Court or registrar
issuing the summons to be likely—

to be able to give material evidence for any
party to the proceeding; or

to have in the person's possession or control
any documents or things which may be
relevant on the hearing of the proceeding; or

both to be able to give material evidence and
to have in the person's possession or control
any relevant documents or things.

A witness summons must require the person to
whom it is directed to attend at a specified venue
of the Court on a certain date and at a certain
time—
to give evidence in the proceeding; or

to produce for examination at the hearing
any documents or things described in the
summons that are in the person's possession
or control; or

both to give evidence and produce for
examination any documents or things
described in the summons that are in the
person's possession or control.

A witness summons must be served a reasonable
time before the day on which the proceeding is
listed before the Court.

history.raw: S. 43(5) substituted by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 82.27).

nodes.text: A witness summons must be served by—

history.raw: S. 43(5A) inserted by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 82.27).

nodes.text:
giving a copy of the summons to the person
to be served; or

if the person does not accept the copy,
putting the copy down in the person's
presence and telling the person the nature of
the summons; or

leaving a copy of the summons for the
person at the person's last known or usual
place of residence or business with a person
who appears to be of or over the age of
16 years.

If the person to be served is a company or
registered body (within the meaning of the
Corporations Act), a witness summons may be
served on the company or body in accordance
with section 109X or 601CX of that Act, as the
case requires.

history.raw: S. 43(5B) inserted by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 82.27).

nodes.text:
A person to whom a witness summons is directed
is, subject to subsection (7), excused from
complying with the summons unless conduct
money is given or tendered to the person at the
time of service of the summons or a reasonable
time before the return date.

It is not necessary to give or tender conduct
money to a person to whom a witness summons is
directed if the person will not reasonably incur
any expenses in complying with the summons.

The Court may direct that a witness who has
attended before the Court in answer to a witness
summons is entitled to receive from the party who
applied for the issue of the witness summons
further conduct money for each day of attendance.
Nothing in this section—

derogates from the power of the Court to
certify that a witness be paid his or her
expenses of attending before the Court.

Unless the Court or the registrar issuing the
summons otherwise directs, a summons to
produce documents or things or a summons to
give evidence and produce documents or things
permits the person to whom the summons is
directed, instead of producing the document or
thing at the hearing, to produce it, together with a
copy of the summons, to the appropriate registrar
not later than 2 days before the first day on which
production is required.

If a document or thing is produced to the
appropriate registrar under subsection (1), he or
she must—

if requested to do so, give a receipt to the
person producing the document or thing; and

produce the document or thing as the Court
directs.

The production of a document or thing to the
appropriate registrar under subsection (1) in
answer to a summons to give evidence and
produce documents or things does not remove the
requirement on the person to whom the summons
is directed to attend for the purpose of giving
evidence.

history.raw: S. 45 amended by No. 11/2021 s. 55 (ILA s. 39B(1)).

nodes.text:
A person whose attendance before the Court in a
criminal proceeding has been required by witness
summons must—
until excused by the Court.

subject to section 43(6), attend at the time
and place specified in the summons; and

if the proceeding is adjourned, attend at the
time and place to which the proceeding has
been adjourned, without the issue of a further
summons—

A witness is not required to attend court on the
date and time specified in a witness summons
under subsection (1)(a), if the criminal proceeding
is adjourned prior to the date and time specified in
that summons.

history.raw: S. 45(2) inserted by No. 11/2021 s. 55.

nodes.heading: Power to amend where there is a defect or error

nodes.text:
On the hearing of a proceeding the Court must
not allow an objection to a warrant on account of
any defect or error in it in substance or in form or
for any variance between it and the evidence
presented in the proceeding but the Court may
amend the warrant to correct the defect or error.

history.raw: S. 50(1) amended by No. 7/2009 s. 427(1)(e) (as amended by No. 68/2009 s. 54(m)).

nodes.text:
An order must not be set aside or quashed only
because of a defect or error in form but the Court
may amend the order to correct the defect or error.

history.raw: Pt 4 Div. 3 Subdiv. 7 (Heading and ss 82A–82F) inserted by No. 33/1994 s. 11(1), amended by Nos 45/1996 s. 18(Sch. 2 item 9.4), 70/1996 s. 7, 84/1997 s. 52, 99/2000 s. 3, 3/2005 s. 26, repealed by No. 12/2006 s. 176(1).
Pt 4 Div. 3 Subdiv. 8 (Heading and ss 82G–82I) inserted by No. 99/2000 s. 4.
S. 57(10) repealed by No. 38/2017 s. 71.

nodes.text: The following warrants may be issued—
warrant to arrest;
remand warrant;
search warrant;
warrant to seize property;
warrant to imprison;
warrant to detain in a youth justice centre;

history.raw: S. 57(1)(f) amended by No. 48/2006 s. 42(Sch. item 22.4).

nodes.text: enforcement warrant.

history.raw: S. 57(1)(g) inserted by No. 33/1994 s. 9(1), substituted by No. 32/2006 s. 88(2), amended by No. 47/2014 s. 271.

nodes.text:
A warrant may be issued in paper form or
electronically in accordance with this Division.

history.raw: S. 57(1AA) inserted by No. 33/2018 s. 50(1).

nodes.text:
A warrant may be issued electronically by the
person issuing the warrant causing the warrant,
or the prescribed particulars of the warrant, to be
transmitted electronically to the person to whom
the warrant is issued in accordance with the
regulations, if any.

history.raw: S. 57(1A) inserted by No. 3/2016 s. 4(1), substituted by No. 33/2018 s. 50(2).

nodes.text:
A warrant issued in accordance with
subsection (1A)—

history.raw: S. 57(1B) inserted by No. 3/2016 s. 4(1).

nodes.text:
directs and authorises the person to whom it
is issued to do all things that the person
would have been directed or authorised to do
if a warrant containing the particulars
referred to in subsection (1A) had been
issued in paper form under subsection (1) by
the person issuing the warrant; and

must not be amended, altered or varied after
its issue, unless the amendment, alteration or
variation is authorised by or under this Act
or any other Act.

The person issuing a warrant must cause the
prescribed particulars of the warrant to be entered
in the register.

A warrant must name or otherwise describe the
person or property against whom or which it is
issued.

All warrants, other than a search warrant, may be
issued by a registrar, a judicial registrar or a
magistrate.

A search warrant may only be issued by a
magistrate.
Remand warrants may be issued by a bail justice.

A judge of the Supreme Court or judge of the
County Court may exercise any power conferred
on a magistrate by or under this Act with respect
to the issue, recall or cancellation of a warrant or
duplicate copy of a warrant.

The registrar of the County Court, the
Prothonotary of the Supreme Court or the
Registrar of Criminal Appeals, as the case
requires, may issue a warrant to imprison in the
circumstances set out in sections 263(4), 266(3A)
and 267(1A) of the Criminal Procedure
Act 2009.

The registrar of the County Court, the
Prothonotary of the Supreme Court or the
Registrar of Criminal Appeals, as the case
requires, may issue a warrant to detain in a youth
justice centre or a youth residential centre in the
circumstances set out in sections 430(4), 430C(5)
and 430D(1A) of the Children, Youth and
Families Act 2005.

A warrant must be executed by the use of a copy
of the warrant, known as the execution copy, or by
the use of a copy of the execution copy, including
a copy transmitted by facsimile machine or other
means of electronic communication.

history.raw: S. 57(8) amended by No. 3/2016 s. 4(2).

nodes.text:
The execution copy of a warrant must be in
writing and, subject to subsection (1A), must be
signed or otherwise authenticated by the person
issuing it.

history.raw: S. 57(9) amended by No. 3/2016 s. 4(3).

nodes.heading: Warrants to arrest issued under Evidence Act 2008
nodes.text:
The provisions of this Division relating to
warrants to arrest extend and apply to a warrant
to arrest issued under section 194 of the Evidence
Act 2008 except as otherwise provided in this
Division.

history.raw: S. 57A inserted by No. 69/2009 s. 54(Sch. Pt 1 item 34.4).

nodes.text:
A warrant issued by a registrar, judicial registrar,
magistrate or bail justice may be recalled and
cancelled by2—

history.raw: S. 58(1) amended by No. 33/2018 s. 51(a).

nodes.text:
that registrar, judicial registrar, magistrate or
bail justice; or

history.raw: S. 58(1)(a) amended by No. 33/2018 s. 51(b).

nodes.text:
if issued by a judicial registrar, any other
judicial registrar; or

history.raw: S. 58(1)(ab) inserted by No. 17/2023 s. 37.

nodes.text:
if issued by a registrar, the registrar for the
time being at the venue of the Court at which
it was issued or, except in the case of an
enforcement warrant issued under the Fines
Reform Act 2014, any other registrar; or

history.raw: S. 58(1)(b) amended by Nos 44/1997 s. 29, 12/2006 s. 169(d), substituted by No. 47/2014 s. 272(1).

nodes.text: a magistrate.

If a warrant has been recalled and cancelled under
subsection (1), a fresh warrant may be issued for
the same purpose as that for which the recalled
warrant was issued.

history.raw: S. 58(1A) inserted by No. 70/1996 s. 4.

nodes.text:
A warrant to imprison or detain in a youth justice
centre for non-payment of a fine (whether issued
before or after the commencement of this section)
is null and void if it has not been executed within
the period of 5 years after a warrant of that type
was first issued against the person named in the
warrant for the purpose specified in the
warrant3,4,5.

If a warrant referred to in subsection (2) becomes
null and void under that subsection, the fine in
respect of which it was issued, together with any
associated fees and costs, ceases to be enforceable
or recoverable if no part of the fine had been paid
before the date on which the warrant became null
and void.

history.raw: S. 58(2A) inserted by No. 70/1996 s. 5(2).

nodes.text:
Nothing in subsection (2) or (2A) prevents the
issue, with the leave of the Court, of a fresh
warrant for the same purpose as that for which a
warrant that has become null and void under
subsection (2) was issued6.

Despite subsection (2), if under subsection (3) a
fresh warrant is issued, the fine in respect of
which it was issued, together with any associated
fees and costs, again becomes enforceable or
recoverable as if there had been no cessation.

history.raw: S. 58(4) inserted by No. 70/1996 s. 5(4).

nodes.text:
If the execution copy of a warrant issued by a
registrar, judicial registrar, magistrate or bail
justice is lost or destroyed before it is executed, a
registrar, judicial registrar or magistrate may issue
a duplicate execution copy if satisfied by evidence
on oath or affirmation or by affidavit of the loss or
destruction of the execution copy of the warrant.

A duplicate execution copy must bear on its face
the word "Duplicate" and may be executed in all
respects as if it were the execution copy of the
warrant.

When a duplicate execution copy of a warrant is
issued, the execution copy of the warrant becomes
null and void and must, if located, be returned to
the principal registrar.

If a person is in a prison, a police gaol or a youth
justice centre in accordance with a warrant which
has been executed, or having been released on
parole from a prison, a police gaol or a youth
justice centre is still under sentence, and the
execution copy of the warrant is lost or destroyed,
a registrar, judicial registrar or magistrate may
issue a duplicate execution copy if satisfied by
evidence on oath or affirmation or by affidavit of
the loss or destruction of the execution copy.

A duplicate execution copy issued under
subsection (4) is sufficient authority for the person
in whose legal custody the person is, or into
whose legal custody the person is delivered, to
keep the person in the prison, police gaol or youth
justice centre until the end of the term specified in
the warrant.

nodes.heading: Effect of defect or error in certain warrants

nodes.text:
A warrant to imprison, a warrant to detain in a
youth justice centre, a remand warrant, a warrant
to seize property or an enforcement warrant7 is not
void only because of a defect or error in it if there
is a valid order supporting it.

A person acting under a warrant to seize property
or an enforcement warrant8 is not to be taken to be
a trespasser from the beginning only because of a
defect or error in it.

history.raw: S. 61(4) repealed by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 82.30).
Note to s. 61 inserted by No. 69/2009 s. 54(Sch. Pt 1 item 34.6).

nodes.text:
A warrant to arrest in the first instance may be
issued—

history.raw: S. 61(1)(a) repealed by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 82.29).
S. 61(1)(b) repealed by No. 69/2009 s. 54(Sch. Pt 1 item 34.5).

nodes.text: as authorised by any other Act.

history.raw: S. 61(5)(c) repealed by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 82.31).

nodes.text:
An application for a warrant to arrest in the first
instance must be supported by evidence on oath or
affirmation or by affidavit.

history.raw: S. 61(2) amended by No. 6/2018 s. 68(Sch. 2 item 81.1).

nodes.text:
An affidavit supporting an application for a
warrant to arrest in the first instance may be a
copy of an affidavit transmitted by facsimile
machine or other means of electronic
communication.

history.raw: S. 61(3) amended by No. 3/2016 s. 5.

nodes.text:
A warrant to arrest other than in the first instance
may be issued—

history.raw: S. 61(5)(a) repealed by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 82.31).
S. 61(5)(b) repealed by No. 69/2009 s. 54(Sch. Pt 1 item 34.5).

nodes.text: as authorised by this or any other Act.

A warrant to arrest other than in the first instance
must include a statement of the reason for issuing
the warrant.

Section 194 of the Evidence Act 2008 provides for issuing
warrants to arrest a witness who fails to appear.

The person issuing a warrant to arrest against any
person may endorse the warrant with a direction
that that person must on arrest be released on bail
as specified in the endorsement.

An endorsement under subsection (1) must fix the
amounts in which the principal and the bail
guarantors, if any, are to be bound and the amount
of any money or the value of any security to be
deposited.

This section does not apply in respect of a warrant
authorised to be issued under section 194 of the
Evidence Act 2008.

history.raw: S. 62(3) inserted by No. 69/2009 s. 54(Sch. Pt 1 item 34.7).

nodes.heading: Persons to whom warrant to arrest may be directed

nodes.text: A warrant to arrest may be directed to—
a named police officer; or

history.raw: S. 63(1)(a) amended by No. 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 101.2(a)(i)).

nodes.text: generally all police officers; or

history.raw: S. 63(1)(b) amended by No. 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 101.2(a)(ii)).

nodes.text:
any other person authorised by law to
execute a warrant to arrest.

A warrant to arrest directed to a named police
officer may be executed by any police officer.

history.raw: S. 63(2) substituted by No. 43/2011 s. 35, amended by No. 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 101.2(b)), substituted by No. 39/2019 s. 14(1).

nodes.text:
A warrant to arrest directed to a named police
officer or to generally all police officers may be
executed by any protective services officer.

history.raw: S. 63(2A) inserted by No. 39/2019 s. 14(1).

nodes.text:
If a protective services officer arrests a person
under subsection (2A), the protective services
officer must hand the person into the custody of a
police officer as soon as practicable after the
person is arrested.

history.raw: S. 63(3) inserted by No, 43/2011 s. 35, amended by Nos 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 101.2(b)), 39/2019 s. 14(2).

nodes.heading: Authority conferred by warrant to arrest

nodes.text:
A warrant to arrest authorises the person to whom
it is directed—

to break, enter and search any place where
the person named or described in the warrant
is suspected to be; and

history.raw: S. 64(2)(a) amended by No. 49/1990 s. 5(a).

nodes.text:
to arrest the person named or described in
the warrant.

The person to whom a warrant to arrest is directed
must cause the person named or described in the
warrant when arrested—

history.raw: Note to s. 64(2) inserted by No. 26/2017 s. 24(1).

nodes.text:
to be brought before a bail justice or the
Court within a reasonable time of being
arrested to be dealt with according to law; or

to be released on bail in accordance with the
endorsement on the warrant.

Section 10A or 12 of the Bail Act 1977 applies on a
person being brought before a bail justice or the Court
at the expiration of the reasonable time referred to in
subsection (2)(a).

A person arrested on a warrant to arrest may be
discharged from custody on bail in accordance
with the Bail Act 1977.

In determining what constitutes a reasonable
time for the purposes of subsection (2)(a) the
matters specified in section 464A(4) of the
Crimes Act 1958 may be considered.

history.raw: S. 64(4) inserted by No. 49/1990 s. 5(b).

nodes.text:
If a person is brought before a bail justice or the
Court in accordance with subsection (2)(a), the
bail justice or the Court is not bound by the
endorsement on the warrant when determining
any matter in relation to bail.

history.raw: S. 64(4A) inserted by No. 70/2010 s. 27(1).

nodes.text:
Subsections (2), (3), (4) and (4A) do not apply in
respect of a warrant authorised to be issued under
section 194 of the Evidence Act 2008.

history.raw: S. 64(5) inserted by No. 69/2009 s. 54(Sch. Pt 1 item 34.8), amended by No. 70/2010 s. 27(2).

nodes.heading: Arrest of person against whom warrant to arrest is issued

nodes.text:
If a warrant to arrest a person who is an accused to
a charge has been issued, any police officer, or
any protective services officer on duty at a
designated place, may arrest the person although
the execution copy of the warrant is not at the
time in the police officer's or protective services
officer's possession.

If a protective services officer arrests a person
under subsection (1), the protective services
officer must hand the person into the custody of a
police officer as soon as practicable after the
person is arrested.

history.raw: S. 65(1A) inserted by No. 43/2011 s. 36(2), amended by No. 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 101.3(b)).

nodes.text:
A protective services officer may only exercise
the power to arrest under this section in relation to
a person who is at, or in the vicinity of, a
designated place.

history.raw: S. 65(1B) inserted by No. 45/2017 s. 55.

nodes.text:
On the arrest of a person under subsection (1) by a
police officer or on the handing of a person
arrested by a protective services officer into the
custody of a police officer under subsection (1A),
the police officer must bring the person arrested
before a bail justice or the Court within a
reasonable time of being arrested or handed into
the custody of the police officer (as the case may
be) and the bail justice or the Court may—

if a fresh charge-sheet is filed to the effect of
the offence or matter alleged in the
warrant—

history.raw: S. 65(2)(a) amended by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 82.33).

nodes.text: permit the person to go at large; or
admit the person to bail; or

in the case of the Court, hear and
determine the proceeding for the
offence; or

if a fresh charge-sheet is not filed to the
effect of the offence or matter alleged in the
warrant—

history.raw: S. 65(2)(b) amended by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 82.33).

nodes.text: permit the person to go at large; or
admit the person to bail; or

remand the person in custody for a
reasonable time pending execution of
the warrant.

If a person has been arrested under subsection (1)
and has been remanded in custody pending
execution of the warrant and the warrant is not
executed within a reasonable time, the Court must
discharge the person from custody.

If a warrant is executed by use of a copy other
than the execution copy, the Court must—

if satisfied that the copy is a true copy of the
execution copy—

proceed as if the person had been
arrested on the execution copy; and

order that the execution copy be
returned to the principal registrar; or

if not so satisfied, discharge the person from
custody.

If a warrant is not executed and a fresh charge-
sheet charging the offence alleged in the warrant
is filed, the warrant is deemed to be void and of
no effect and the Court must order its return to the
principal registrar.

history.raw: S. 65(5) amended by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 82.34).

nodes.text:
In determining what constitutes a reasonable
time for the purposes of subsection (2) the
matters specified in section 464A(4) of the
Crimes Act 1958 may be considered.

history.raw: S. 65(6) amended by No. 49/1990 s. 5(d).

nodes.heading: Issue of warrant to imprison
nodes.text: A warrant to imprison may be issued if—

the Court orders that a person be sentenced
to a term of imprisonment; or

the Court orders that a person be sentenced
to a term of imprisonment in default of
payment of a fine or of any instalment under
an instalment order; or
authorised by any other Act.

nodes.heading: Persons to whom warrant to imprison may be directed

nodes.text: A warrant to imprison may be directed to—
a named police officer; or

history.raw: S. 69(1)(a) amended by No. 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 101.4(a)(i)).

nodes.text: generally all police officers; or

history.raw: S. 69(1)(b) amended by No. 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 101.4(a)(ii)).

nodes.text: the sheriff; or

history.raw: S. 69(1)(ba) inserted by No. 34/1990 s. 4(Sch. 3 item 5).

history.raw: S. 69(1)(bb) inserted by No. 34/1990 s. 4(Sch. 3 item 5).

any other person authorised by law to
execute a warrant to imprison.

A warrant to imprison directed to a named police
officer may be executed by any police officer.

nodes.text:
A warrant to imprison directed to a named police
officer or to generally all police officers may be
executed by any prison officer.

history.raw: S. 69(3) inserted by No. 34/1990 s. 4(Sch. 3 item 6), amended by No. 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 101.4(c)).

nodes.text:
A warrant to imprison under section 68(b) to be
directed to the sheriff may be issued, not in paper
form, but by a magistrate or registrar signing a
document containing the following particulars in
relation to persons against whom a warrant is to
be issued under that section and causing those
particulars to be transferred electronically to the
sheriff in accordance with the regulations, if
any—

history.raw: S. 69(3A) inserted by No. 69/1997 s. 28(1).

nodes.text: the name of the person in default;
the type of warrant;

the amount of the fine or instalment
remaining unpaid;
the date of issue of the warrant;

the name of the magistrate or registrar
signing the document;
any other particulars that are prescribed.

A warrant issued in accordance with
subsection (3A)—

history.raw: S. 69(3B) inserted by No. 69/1997 s. 28(1).

nodes.text:
directs and authorises the sheriff to do all
things that he or she would have been
directed and authorised to do if a warrant
containing the particulars referred to in
subsection (3A) and directed to the sheriff
had been issued in paper form under
section 68(b) by the magistrate or registrar;

must not be amended, altered or varied after
its issue, unless the amendment, alteration or
variation is authorised by or under this or
any other Act.

Subsections (4) to (7) of section 111 apply to a
warrant to imprison directed to the sheriff under
this Subdivision in the same manner as they apply
to a warrant to seize property directed to the
sheriff in a civil proceeding.

history.raw: S. 69(4) inserted by No. 34/1990 s. 4(Sch. 3 item 6).

nodes.heading: Directions in, and authority of, warrant to imprison
nodes.text: A warrant to imprison—

authorises the person to whom it is directed
to break, enter and search any place where
the person named in the warrant is suspected
to be; and

directs and authorises the person to whom it
is directed to take and safely convey the
person named in the warrant—
and there to deliver the person to the officer
in charge of the prison or police gaol; and

history.raw: S. 70(b)(iii) repealed by No. 33/1994 s. 9(5).

nodes.text: to a prison; or

history.raw: S. 70(b)(ii) amended by No. 74/2000 s. 3(Sch. 1 item 75).

nodes.text:
directs and authorises the Secretary to the
Department of Justice or the Chief
Commissioner of Police (as the case
requires) or any other person into whose
custody the person named in the warrant is
transferred to receive that person into
custody and safely keep that person—

history.raw: S. 70(c) amended by No. 45/1996 s. 18(Sch. 2 item 9.1).

nodes.text:
for the period specified, or in the
circumstances described, in the
warrant; or

until that person is otherwise removed
or discharged from custody by due
course of law.

nodes.heading: Reduction of imprisonment by payment of portion of fine

nodes.text:
If before the issue of a warrant to imprison for
non-payment of a fine, it appears to the person
issuing the warrant that part of the fine has been
paid—

the reduction in the amount of the fine
payable must be stated in the warrant to
imprison; and

the term for which the person fined may be
imprisoned must be reduced by the number
of days bearing as nearly as possible the
same proportion to the total number of days
in the term as the amount paid bears to the
whole amount of the fine.

Subsection (1) applies despite any provision
(except section 26) of the Imprisonment of
Fraudulent Debtors Act 1958 to the contrary.

If after the issue but before the execution of a
warrant to imprison for non-payment of a fine, it
appears to the Court that part of the fine has been
paid, the Court must—
in accordance with subsection (1).
amend the warrant; and

recall the execution copy of the warrant and
amend it—

Despite any provision (except section 26) of
the Imprisonment of Fraudulent Debtors
Act 1958 to the contrary or anything in any
warrant to imprison, if a person is imprisoned
for non-payment of a fine—

the whole or any part of the fine may be paid
by or on behalf of that person to the officer
in charge of the prison or police gaol in
which that person is detained; and

the officer in charge must receive the
payment and forward it without delay to the
principal registrar.

If—
is paid to the officer in charge of the prison or
police gaol by or on behalf of the person
imprisoned, the person imprisoned must be
discharged if he or she is in custody for no other
matter.
the whole amount of the fine; or
the amount remaining to be paid—

If part of the fine is paid to the officer in charge of
the prison or police gaol by or on behalf of the
person imprisoned—

the term of imprisonment for non-payment
of the fine must be reduced having regard to
the formula set out in subsection (1)(b); and
the officer in charge must—

amend the execution copy of the
warrant; and

at the end of the reduced term, the person
imprisoned must be discharged if he or she is
in custody for no other matter.

nodes.heading: Provisions extend to detention in youth justice centre
nodes.text:
If a person is directed under Subdivision (4) of
Division 2 of Part 3 of the Sentencing Act 1991
or under the Children, Youth and Families
Act 2005 to be detained in a youth justice centre
or a youth residential centre, the provisions of this
Subdivision and of any regulations with respect to
warrants to imprison extend and apply, with any
necessary modifications, with respect to the issue
and execution of a warrant to detain in a youth
justice centre or a youth residential centre and
with respect to any matter arising out of any such
detention.

history.raw: S. 72 (Heading) inserted by No. 48/2006 s. 42(Sch. item 22.5).
S. 73(3A)(3B) inserted by No. 70/1996 s. 6, repealed by No. 12/2006 s. 169(e).

nodes.text: A warrant to seize property may be issued—

if the accused in a criminal proceeding in the
Court fails to comply with an order for the
payment of a fine or of any instalment under
an instalment order; or

a named police officer; or

the sheriff; or

nodes.text:
any other person authorised by law to

police officer may be executed by any police

subsection (1)(a) or section 98(7)(b) to be

to be transferred electronically to the sheriff in

the amount of the fine or instalment

the date of issue of the warrant;

the name of the magistrate or registrar

any other particulars that are prescribed.

A warrant issued in accordance with

nodes.text:
directs and authorises the sheriff to do all
things that he or she would have been
directed and authorised to do if a warrant
containing the particulars referred to in

had been issued in paper form under

must not be amended, altered or varied after

under this Subdivision in the same manner as they

nodes.heading: Authority conferred by warrant to seize property
nodes.text:
A warrant to seize property directs and authorises
the person to whom it is directed—

to seize the personal property of the person
named or described in the warrant; and

if the sums named in the warrant together
with all lawful costs of execution are not
paid, to sell the personal property seized.

A search warrant may be issued as authorised by
any Act other than this Act.

An application for a search warrant must be
supported by evidence on oath or by affirmation
or by affidavit.

history.raw: S. 75(2) amended by No. 6/2018 s. 68(Sch. 2 item 81.3).

nodes.text:
An affidavit supporting an application for a search
warrant may be a copy of an affidavit transmitted
by facsimile machine or other means of electronic
communication.

history.raw: S. 75(3) amended by No. 3/2016 s. 6.

nodes.heading: Persons to whom search warrant may be directed

nodes.text: A search warrant may be directed to—
a named police officer; or

history.raw: S. 76(1)(a) amended by No. 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 101.6(a)(i)).

nodes.text: generally all police officers; or

history.raw: S. 76(1)(b) amended by No. 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 101.6(a)(ii)).

nodes.text:
any other person authorised by law to
execute a search warrant.

A search warrant directed to a named police
officer may be executed by any police officer.

history.raw: S. 76(2) amended by No. 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 101.6(b)).

nodes.text:
The person issuing a search warrant may endorse
the warrant with a direction that any person
arrested must be released on bail as specified in
the endorsement.

An endorsement under subsection (1) must fix the
amounts in which the principal and the bail
guarantors, if any, are to be bound and the amount
of any money or the value of any security to be
deposited.

A search warrant authorises the person to whom it
is directed—

where the person named or described in

to arrest the person named or described
in the warrant; and
if the warrant is to search for any thing—

to break, enter and search any place or
vehicle named or described in the
warrant for any article, thing or
material of any kind named or
described in the warrant; and

to bring the article, thing or material
before the Court so that the matter may
be dealt with according to law; and

to arrest any person apparently having
possession, custody or control of the
article, thing or material.

The person to whom a search warrant is directed
must cause the person named or described in the

or control of any article, thing or material named
or described in the warrant, when arrested—

nodes.text:
to be brought before a bail justice or the

to be released on bail in accordance with the

Section 10A or 12 of the Bail Act 1977 applies on a
person being brought before a bail justice or the Court
at the expiration of the reasonable time referred to in
subsection (2)(a).

A person arrested on a search warrant may be
discharged from custody on bail in accordance
with the Bail Act 1977.

In determining what constitutes a reasonable

history.raw: S. 78(4) inserted by No. 49/1990 s. 5(f).

history.raw: S. 78(4A) inserted by No. 70/2010 s. 28.

nodes.text:
For the purposes of subsection (1)(b)(ii) an article,

nodes.text:

vehicle includes motor vehicle, aircraft and vessel.

if an accused has been committed to stand

a named police officer; or

if the Court has given a direction under

Power to assist police at road checks

history.raw: S. 82I inserted by No. 99/2000 s. 4.

nodes.text:
This section applies if a police officer exercising a
power conferred (whether directly or by
implication) by the Road Safety Act 1986 or the
Heavy Vehicle National Law (Victoria) requests
or signals the driver of a motor vehicle to stop the
vehicle.

history.raw: S. 82I(1) amended by Nos 30/2013 s. 60(Sch. item 7), 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 101.8).

nodes.text:
Once the vehicle has stopped, the police officer or
any person who is a bailiff for the purposes of the
Supreme Court Act 1986 (other than a bailiff
who is a sheriff's officer) may direct the driver of
the vehicle—
to enable a determination of whether the driver, or
any person accompanying the driver, is named in

history.raw: Note to s. 82I(2) inserted by No. 9/2009 s. 75(2).

nodes.text: to keep the vehicle stationary;
to drive the vehicle to a designated spot;

to produce his or her driver licence document
or permit document;

to comply with any other reasonable

nodes.heading: Imprisonment in default of payment of fine

history.raw: S. 97(2) repealed by No. 49/1991 s. 119(7) (Sch. 4 item 13.6).

nodes.text:
If the Court makes an order in a proceeding
imposing a fine and the person fined is not present
when the order is made—

the principal registrar must cause to be sent
by post to the person fined, at the address
appearing on the charge-sheet or any later
address notified to the Court by that person,
a notice advising of the order imposing the
fine; and
the fine is payable—

within such longer period as is ordered
by the Court under a time to pay order
within the meaning of the Sentencing
Act 1991.

If in any proceeding the Court orders a
corporation to pay a fine then, despite anything in
this or any other Act, that order may be enforced
by a warrant to seize property.

In this section—
director, in relation to a body corporate, includes
any person occupying the position of director
of the body corporate (by whatever name
called) and includes a person in accordance
with whose directions or instructions the
directors of the body corporate are
accustomed to act;
reciprocating court means a court of a
reciprocating State or Territory declared by
proclamation under this section to be a
reciprocating court;
reciprocating State or Territory means another
State or a Territory of the Commonwealth
that is declared by proclamation under this
section to be a reciprocating State or
Territory.

The Governor in Council may, subject to
subsection (3), declare another State or a Territory
of the Commonwealth to be a reciprocating State
or Territory for the purposes of the enforcement
against a body corporate in Victoria of a fine
payable under an order of a court having summary
jurisdiction in the other State or in the Territory.

A State or Territory the subject of a proclamation
under subsection (2) must have laws providing for
enforcement against a body corporate in that State
or Territory of a fine payable under an order of the
Magistrates' Court or other court having summary
jurisdiction in Victoria.

The Governor in Council may by proclamation
declare a court having summary jurisdiction in a
reciprocating State or Territory to be a
reciprocating court for the purposes of the
enforcement against a body corporate in Victoria
of a fine payable under a conviction or order of
that court.

For the purposes of subsection (4) a court may be
declared singly or in conjunction with another or
others by such description or class or by means of
any reference that the Governor in Council thinks
fit.

If, under an order of a reciprocating court made in
the exercise of its summary jurisdiction—
the registrar must register the order in the
Magistrates' Court by filing in the Court a
certified copy of the order and must note the date
of registration on the copy.

a registrar of the Magistrates' Court at a
venue at or near to a place where the body
corporate has or appears to have property,
receives a request in writing from a registrar
or other corresponding officer of the
reciprocating court for the enforcement of
the order accompanied by—
a certified copy of the order; and

a certificate signed by the registrar or
corresponding officer making the
request certifying the amount of the
fine outstanding under the order—

On the registration of an order under
subsection (6)—

the order is deemed to be an order of the
Magistrates' Court requiring payment by the
body corporate of the amount of the fine
referred to in the certificate under
subsection (6) as outstanding; and

the registrar may issue a warrant to seize
property of the body corporate for the
purpose of recovering the amount of the fine;
and

the warrant issued under paragraph (b) is
deemed to be a warrant to seize property
issued under this Act and the provisions of
this Act, with any necessary modifications,
apply and extend to the enforcement of that
warrant.

If the registrar receives, after the request for the
enforcement of the order, a notification from the
registrar or other corresponding officer of the
reciprocating court of payment by or on behalf of
the body corporate of the whole or part of the
outstanding fine, the registrar must—
if the fine—

has been paid in full, withdraw the
warrant; or

has not been paid in full, amend the
warrant to show the amount still
outstanding, and the warrant may be
enforced in respect of the altered
amount.

The registrar of the Magistrates' Court must remit
to the registrar or other corresponding officer of
the reciprocating court which made the order any
sum of money received in satisfaction of the
whole or part of a fine payable under an order
enforced under subsection (7).

Any sum of money paid to or received by a
registrar of the Magistrates' Court from a
reciprocating court in satisfaction of the whole
or part of a fine payable under an order of the
Magistrates' Court enforced by the reciprocating
court must be paid to or received by and applied
by the registrar as if the sum had been paid to the
registrar by the body corporate by which the fine
was payable.

nodes.heading: Procedure for enforcement of infringement penalties under the Fines Reform Act 2014
Infringement offence enforcement procedure under the Fines Reform Act 2014
nodes.text:
The procedure set out in the Fines Reform
Act 2014 may be used instead of commencing a
proceeding against a person for an offence for
which an infringement notice within the meaning
of the Infringements Act 2006 could be issued or
served in respect of an offence under an Act or
other instrument which establishes the offence.

history.raw: S. 99 amended by No. 70/1996 s. 8, substituted by Nos 12/2006 s. 171 (as amended by No. 32/2006 s. 53(1)), 47/2014 s. 275.

nodes.heading: Certain agencies may give information for enforcement purposes

history.raw: S. 99A inserted by No. 99/2000 s. 5.

nodes.text:
In this section, specified agency means a person
or body—
but does not include a relevant agency within the
meaning of section 69 of the Melbourne City
Link Act 1995.

history.raw: S. 99A(1) amended by No. 8/2019 s. 114.

nodes.text:
that is stated by regulations made for the
purposes of this section to be a specified
agency—

Words and expressions used in this section have
the same meanings as in section 124A.

history.raw: S. 99A(2) amended by No. 12/2006 s. 172(a).

nodes.text:
The registrar, the sheriff and any contractor or
sub-contractor supporting the functions of the
Court under the Fines Reform Act 2014 or the
sheriff may, for the purpose of the enforcement of
court orders and fines, request information that
may assist in carrying out that purpose from any
person or body.

On the written request of the registrar, the sheriff
or any contractor or sub-contractor supporting the
functions of the Court under the Fines Reform
Act 2014 or the sheriff, a specified agency may
give the person or body making the request access
to any information held by the agency that may be
of use in the enforcement of court orders and
fines.

A person who obtains access to any information
as a result of a request made under this section—

may use the information to enforce court
orders and fines; but

is otherwise subject to all the requirements
and restrictions concerning the use and
disclosure of the information that apply to
the person who provided, or granted access
to, the information in response to the request.

The Court has jurisdiction, subject to
subsection (2)—

to hear and determine any cause of action for
damages or a debt or a liquidated demand if
the amount claimed is within the
jurisdictional limit; and

to hear and determine any claim for equitable
relief if the value of the relief sought is
within the jurisdictional limit; and

history.raw: S. 100(6)(b) amended by No. 35/1996 s. 453(Sch. 1 item 53.3).

nodes.text:
to hear and determine, with the consent in
writing of the parties—

any cause of action for damages or a
debt or a liquidated demand,
irrespective of the amount claimed; and

any claim for equitable relief,
irrespective of the value of the relief
sought; and

to hear and determine applications made
under section 57B of the Victorian Civil
and Administrative Tribunal Act 1998;
and

history.raw: S. 100(1)(ca) inserted by No. 31/2021 s. 8(1).

nodes.text:
to hear and determine any other cause of
action if the Court is given jurisdiction to do
so by or under any Act other than this Act.

The Court does not have jurisdiction in any cause
of action—

in which the effect of, or the validity or
invalidity of, any act, matter or thing done or
omitted to be done by any person or body
whatsoever in the exercise or purported
exercise of any power or duty conferred or
imposed on that person or body or
purportedly conferred or imposed on that
person or body by or under—
is sought to be determined or declared; or
any royal prerogative; or
any statute—

in the nature of a proceeding for a
prerogative writ; or

brought on a judgment of the Supreme Court
or the County Court.

The jurisdictional limit does not apply to any
question or matter that the Court has jurisdiction
to determine arising out of any of the following—

history.raw: S. 100(2A) inserted by No. 9/2010 s. 93, amended by No. 67/2013 s. 649(Sch. 9 item 24(1)), substituted by No. 31/2021 s. 8(2).

nodes.text:
Part IV of the Accident Compensation
Act 1985;

Part 3A of the Victorian Civil and
Administrative Tribunal Act 1998;

the Workplace Injury Rehabilitation and
Compensation Act 2013.

For the purpose of determining in a proceeding
involving property whether the amount claimed
or the value of the relief sought is within the
jurisdictional limit, a certificate which purports to
have been issued by a valuer and which purports
to state the value of the property as at a particular
date is admissible in evidence and, in the absence
of evidence to the contrary, is proof of the value
of the property as at that date.

The Court does not cease to have jurisdiction in
respect of a cause of action because—

part of the cause of action arose outside
Victoria—if a material part of it arose in
Victoria; or

the whole cause of action arose outside
Victoria—if the defendant resided within
Victoria at the time of being served with the
complaint.

A minor may bring a proceeding in the Court for
the recovery of money payable to the minor under
a contract of service or a contract for services as if
the minor were of full age.

A party to a civil proceeding (including an
arbitration) may appear—
personally; or

by a legal practitioner or other person
empowered by law to appear for the party; or

in the case of a cause of action for a debt or a
liquidated demand, by a person in the
exclusive employment of the party who is
authorised in writing to appear for the party.

Every judgment debt carries interest at the rate for
the time being fixed under section 2 of the
Penalty Interest Rates Act 1983 from the time
the order was made.

Payment of the interest may be enforced by a
warrant to seize property.

history.raw: S. 100(8) substituted by No. 34/1990 s. 4(Sch. 3 item 11).

nodes.text:
The amount of the interest must be stated in the
body of the warrant.

nodes.text:
If a civil proceeding is wholly or partly beyond
the jurisdiction of the Court, the Court may—

order that the proceeding be stayed pending
the making of an application under Part 3 of
the Courts (Case Transfer) Act 1991; or

order that the complaint be struck out and
award costs as if the Court had jurisdiction
and the complaint were dismissed.

If—
the Court may exercise the power conferred by
subsection (1)(c).

under subsection (1)(b) the Court orders that
a proceeding be stayed pending the making
of an application under Part 3 of the Courts
(Case Transfer) Act 1991; and

within a reasonable time after the making of
that order the proceeding has not been
transferred to another court—

nodes.heading: Court orders relating to administration of children's funds

history.raw: S. 101A inserted by No. 15/1998 s. 9.

nodes.text:
If in any civil proceedings before the Court it is
adjudged or ordered that money be paid to a child
(whether or not that child is a party to a cause or
matter) the money—
is to be paid into court; and

unless the Court otherwise orders, is to be
paid out to an administrator specified by the
Court.

If any money, not being money to which
subsection (3) applies—
the Court may by order direct that the money be
paid out to an administrator specified in the order.
is paid into court—

before the commencement of this
section; or

after the commencement of this
section in accordance with a judgment
or order entered or made before the
commencement of this section; and

the money is being held in court on behalf of
a child—

If the Court adjudges or orders that property
(whether real or personal) be delivered up or
transferred to a child (whether or not that child is
a party to a cause or matter), the Court—

may order that the property be delivered up
or transferred to an administrator specified in
the order; and

may give any directions for the service of the
order on the administrator as it thinks fit.

If an order under subsection (3) is served on State
Trustees within the meaning of the State Trustees
(State Owned Company) Act 1994, State
Trustees must accept delivery or transfer of the
property to which the order relates and the
acceptance of the property is a sufficient discharge
to the person delivering or transferring the
property.

A copy of any order made under this section must
be given by the administrator to VCAT and to the
Public Advocate within the meaning of the
Guardianship and Administration Act 2019.

history.raw: S. 101A(5) amended by No. 30/2004 s. 14(1)(2), substituted by No. 13/2019 s. 221(Sch. 1 item 29.1).

nodes.text:
An order of the Court under this section that
money be paid out to an administrator has effect
as if it were an administration order under the
Guardianship and Administration Act 2019
and, subject to the order of the Court, the
administrator has all the powers and duties set out
